# Archived Presidential White House Websites

White House websites are Presidential records. The official files that make up a Presidential administration's website are preserved in our Executive Office of the President Electronic Records Archive. In order for the public to easily access the websites, the National Archives has taken an additional step to "freeze" the White House websites and make them available online. Because the archived websites are hosted by the National Archives and are historical material, they are no longer updated. Any broken links (internal or external) will not be updated.

The archived websites are an excellent resource for photographs, speeches, press releases, digital data and other public domain records.

## Production Quality and Technical Standards

Government video production teams follow strict technical guidelines to ensure clarity, stability, and consistency across all recordings. High definition formats are now standard for new uploads.

These standards include frame rate, audio normalization, and color calibration, which help archival footage remain usable for long term reference and broadcast reuse.

## History and Evolution of Official Government Videography

The history of White House gov videos reflects advances in broadcast technology and public access policies. Early recordings were distributed on physical media, while modern releases prioritize digital streaming.

Milestones include the transition to web based streaming, the adoption of open captioning, and integration with social media platforms that increase reach while maintaining authenticity.

## FAQ

### Where can I find the most recent official White House videos?

You can find the latest videos on WhiteHouse.gov and its dedicated video portal, which are mirrored on official YouTube and social channels for broader reach.

### Are these videos captioned and available in multiple languages?

Yes, most new recordings include closed captions in English, and agencies often provide Spanish or additional language versions for key addresses.

### How are older White House gov videos preserved and archived?

The National Archives and Records Administration maintains a long term archive, ensuring that historical footage remains accessible in high fidelity.

### Can I use official White House videos for educational or journalistic purposes?

These recordings are in the public domain, allowing use for reporting, teaching, and research with proper attribution to the original source.
